nodes.description: Private uint256 state variable holding the secret number used for guessing.
Public uint256 state variable recording the last time the game was played (set from now).
Public address state variable holding the contract owner, set to msg.sender at construction.
Constant address receiving a 20% share during the kill() payout.
Dynamic array of Player structs recording every participant and their sent value.
Constructor that sets owner from msg.sender and calls shuffle() to initialize secretNumber.
Payable public function accepting a guess, recording the player, paying out the whole balance on a correct guess and re-shuffling.
Internal function deriving secretNumber from keccak256 over block.timestamp and msg.sender (weak randomness).
Owner-only function that transfers 20% of the balance to megaman and 80% to owner.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership, player registration, randomness and payouts.
Miner-influenced block timestamp (now) used as game randomness and activity clock.
Caller-supplied guess parameter of guess(uint256), must be between 0 and 10.
Local Player struct instance in guess() populated with msg.sender and msg.value before being pushed to players.
Local variable in kill() caching address(this).balance before the percentage transfers.
msg.sender.transfer(address(this).balance) inside guess(), an external ETH send that can invoke the recipient's fallback and reenter.
megaman.transfer((balance*20)/100) in kill(), emits a fixed 20% ETH payout to an external address.
owner.transfer((balance*80)/100) in kill(), emits an 80% ETH payout to the owner address.
keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.timestamp, msg.sender)) % 10 + 1 randomness derivation, predictable and manipulable by miners/callers.

edges.reason: Owner state variable is assigned directly from the caller-controlled msg.sender in the constructor.
msg.sender is supplied by the caller to guess() and drives player registration and payout.
lastPlayed is assigned from now (block.timestamp), creating a timestamp dependency.
shuffle() consumes block.timestamp as a source of pseudo-randomness.
shuffle() mixes msg.sender into the randomness derivation, controllable by the caller.
shuffle() writes the derived value into the secretNumber state variable.
The number parameter is read by guess() for range checking and comparison against secretNumber.
The number parameter is compared to secretNumber to decide the payout branch.
The constructor calls shuffle() to initialize the secret number.
guess() reaches the msg.sender.transfer external send when the guess matches the secret number.
The external ETH transfer can invoke the recipient fallback and reenter guess() before state is settled.
msg.sender is the recipient of the balance transfer, allowing a malicious caller to control the external call.
guess() calls shuffle() after each attempt to refresh the secret number.
kill() requires msg.sender to equal owner, an authorization check over caller input.
The owner state variable is the authority used by the kill() ownership check.
kill() performs the megaman.transfer payout to the constant address.
kill() performs the owner.transfer payout to the owner address.
The cached balance is scaled by 20/100 to compute the megaman transfer amount, an unchecked multiplication.
The cached balance is scaled by 80/100 to compute the owner transfer amount, an unchecked multiplication.
The megaman constant address is the recipient of the 20% transfer.
The owner state variable is the recipient of the 80% transfer.
The local Player struct addr field is filled from msg.sender before being pushed to players.
guess() constructs and pushes the local Player struct as part of its execution.
shuffle() invokes the keccak256-based randomness computation over block.timestamp and msg.sender.
The weak randomness result is truncated modulo 10 and written to secretNumber.

normalization_plan.reason: The number parameter exists only to serve the guess() function's validation and comparison logic.
The local Player struct is a transient construction inside guess() before being appended to players.
The balance local variable is a transient cache used solely inside kill() for the percentage payouts.
